hero.titleLine2: to Claude, Cursor, any MCP client
hero.lead: Xtra Mail takes a plain password over IMAP, with no app password to generate and no second factor in the way. mcpemails connects it so your AI agent can read, search, send, reply and file that mail.
hero.answer: Claude cannot reach an Xtra Mail inbox on its own. mcpemails is a hosted MCP server that connects it over IMAP at imap.xtra.co.nz on port 993, signing in with your full xtra.co.nz address and your ordinary Xtra Mail password. Spark issues no app-specific passwords for Xtra Mail and states that its two-step verification applies only in the webmail portal and not to email clients, so a correct password authenticates directly even with two-step turned on. Once connected, Claude, Cursor or any other MCP client can read, search, send and organise that mail. One inbox is free, forever.

method.title: How Xtra Mail connects: IMAP with the password you already have
method.body: Spark publishes imap.xtra.co.nz on port 993 for incoming mail and send.xtra.co.nz for outgoing, with the username given as the full address. Authentication is the mailbox password, unmodified. That is unusual enough in 2026 to be worth stating twice, because Spark's own two-step verification page carries a note at the top saying it is only available in the webmail portal and will not apply to email clients like Outlook, Mail and Gmail. So there is no app password to find, no security page to visit and no second factor to work around, and the entire failure surface reduces to whether the password is right and whether your client meets Spark's transport requirements. Spark does have those: it asks that the app support 1024-bit or 2048-bit AES ciphers and TLS 1.0 or higher, and states that RC4, SSL and SSL3 are not supported.

setup.p: Sign up at mcpemails.com. The free plan connects one inbox and does not ask for a card.

setup.h: Make sure the Xtra Mail subscription is active in MySpark
setup.p: Xtra Mail is a subscription rather than an automatic extra. In MySpark, open Subscriptions under Products, and check that Xtra Mail is there and activated with a mailbox created. If it says Ready to activate, finish that first; there is no mailbox to connect until the create mailbox form is completed.

setup.h: Enter the full address and your Xtra Mail password
setup.p: In mcpemails choose IMAP / SMTP and enter the address exactly as Spark writes it, such as joe.bloggs@xtra.co.nz, with the password you use to sign in to Xtra webmail. The hosts and ports below are prefilled and were verified from a live TLS connection.

setup.h: Paste the MCP URL into your AI
setup.p: Drop https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp into Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT, authorise, and your agent has the inbox.

gotchas.h: Xtra Mail has not been a Yahoo service since 2017, so Yahoo advice does not apply
gotchas.p: Spark moved Xtra email off Yahoo and onto the New Zealand provider SMX in 2017, migrating hundreds of thousands of mailboxes over about three months. The Yahoo era left a long tail of guides telling xtra.co.nz users to generate a Yahoo app password or to sign in through a Yahoo window. None of that is true any more. There is no Yahoo account behind an Xtra address, and following those instructions leaves you hunting for a security page that does not exist for your mailbox.

gotchas.h: Two-step verification protects webmail only, and does not lock out a client
gotchas.p: Spark's own two-step verification page states in a note at the top that it is only available in the webmail portal and will not apply to email clients like Outlook, Mail and Gmail. That cuts both ways. It means turning two-step on does not break this connection and you never need an app password, and it means the IMAP door stays password-only whatever you set in webmail. Treat the Xtra Mail password accordingly.

gotchas.h: Spark documents port 587 for sending, and port 465 also answers
gotchas.p: Spark's setup page lists the outgoing server as send.xtra.co.nz on port 587 with StartTLS. The connection we verified on that same host is port 465 with implicit TLS, which completed a handshake and offered PLAIN and LOGIN. Both are real. The table on this page shows what we tested; if a client insists on the documented combination, 587 with STARTTLS is Spark's published answer and should also work.

gotchas.h: No SASL-IR, no IDLE, no MOVE and no SPECIAL-USE
gotchas.p: The Xtra server advertises a short list: IMAP4rev1, UIDPLUS, NAMESPACE, ID, and the PLAIN and LOGIN mechanisms. Without SASL-IR it refuses the one-step authentication most clients try first, which comes back as a bare refusal that reads like a wrong password. Without IDLE there is no push, so new mail is found by polling. Without MOVE, filing runs as COPY, then STORE, then EXPUNGE. Without SPECIAL-USE, Sent and Trash are matched by name. UIDPLUS is present, so a copied message does report its new id.

limits: Spark's SMTP host announces a maximum message size of about 100 MB, which is generous, but a larger send is still refused before it leaves.
No IDLE, so new mail is discovered by polling rather than pushed.
Moves are not atomic and folder roles are matched by name, because MOVE and SPECIAL-USE are not implemented on this server.

faq.q: Does Claude work with Xtra Mail?
faq.a: Not directly. Claude has no built-in Spark or Xtra connector. Connecting an MCP server such as mcpemails to the mailbox over IMAP gives Claude read, search, send, reply, schedule and organise access to your xtra.co.nz mail, and the same connection works in Cursor, ChatGPT and other MCP clients.

faq.q: What are the Xtra Mail IMAP and SMTP settings?
faq.a: IMAP is imap.xtra.co.nz on port 993 with TLS. Outgoing mail is send.xtra.co.nz, which Spark documents on port 587 with StartTLS and which also answers on port 465 with implicit TLS, the combination we verified. The username is your full email address. Spark documents pop3.xtra.co.nz on 995 as the POP alternative.

faq.q: Do I need an app password for Xtra Mail?
faq.a: No. Spark issues none, and its two-step verification page says the feature is only available in the webmail portal and will not apply to email clients. A mail client signs in with your ordinary Xtra Mail password whether or not two-step verification is switched on for webmail.

Spark, on a platform supplied by the New Zealand company SMX. Xtra email was hosted by Yahoo from the Telecom NZ era until Spark completed the migration to SMX in 2017. That is why Yahoo-specific instructions still circulating for xtra.co.nz addresses no longer lead anywhere useful.

faq.q: Is my Xtra mail stored on your servers?
faq.a: No. Messages are fetched live from Spark over IMAP for each request and passed to your AI client. Credentials are encrypted at rest and message bodies are not retained.
